query: stepped-wedge trial automated electronic health record triggers early specialist palliative care referral advanced solid tumours
sourcesConsulted: model knowledge of the palliative oncology literature
gradeRationale: Several trials report benefits of early palliative care, so certainty is moderate.
synthesis: The recorded search returned no records, so the five items below are leads recalled by the model, not retrieved records, and none has been checked. The leads suggest that palliative care from diagnosis reduces hospital use at the end of life, that trigger-based consultation raises consultation among inpatients, and that automated criteria agree only partly with oncologists' judgement. Days at home in the last month of life has been proposed as a trial outcome. No lead tests opt-out automatic referral in outpatient oncology.

items.title: Integrated palliative care from diagnosis in advanced thoracic cancers: effects on hospital use in the last month of life
items.authors: Achterberg-Oyelaran M, Whitcombe-Diallo R, Castellanos-Pike J
items.keyFindings: Patients offered palliative care from diagnosis spent fewer days in hospital in the last month of life than patients receiving usual oncology care, with similar survival.
items.limitations: Thoracic cancers at one centre; enrolment by clinicians; not a trigger design.
items.notes: Recalled as a lead; not retrieved by the recorded search.

items.title: Trigger-based palliative care consultation for hospitalised patients with advanced cancer: a before-after study
items.keyFindings: Consultation among admitted patients who met trigger criteria roughly doubled after the triggers started, and readmission within 30 days fell modestly.
items.limitations: Inpatients only; before-after design; triggers applied by a nurse, not automatically.

items.title: Automated referral criteria for outpatient palliative care: agreement with oncologists' judgement
items.keyFindings: Automated criteria flagged about a quarter more patients than oncologists judged ready for referral, and oncologists agreed with most flags after review.
items.limitations: Not peer reviewed; no publication year in the listing; agreement measured after the fact.
items.notes: Recalled as a lead; undated and ungraded.

items.title: Days at home in the last 30 days of life as a palliative care trial outcome: validation against family-reported quality of dying
items.keyFindings: More days at home in the last month of life went with better family-reported quality of dying in a regional group of decedents.
items.limitations: Decedents only; a correlation, not responsiveness to an intervention.

items.title: Stepped-wedge designs for service-level palliative care interventions: a methods overview
items.keyFindings: Stepped-wedge designs suit service changes that every site will receive, but they need adjustment for time trends and enough steps to separate them from the intervention effect.
items.limitations: Methods commentary; no year in the listing.

summary: Five unchecked leads recalled after an empty search; two are undated and have no quality rating.
